summary.short: EU regulation establishing a Cyber Solidarity framework: National and Cross-Border Cyber Hubs for threat detection, an EU Cybersecurity Reserve of trusted managed security service providers for incident response, and an ENISA-run incident review mechanism, funded through the Digital Europe Programme. Applies from the twentieth day after Official Journal publication.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2025/38 (Cyber Solidarity Act) amends Regulation (EU) 2021/694 and sets up three pillars funded through the Digital Europe Programme. First, a European Cybersecurity Alert System: Member States may designate National Cyber Hubs (Art. 4), and at least three Member States may form a Hosting Consortium to establish a Cross-Border Cyber Hub (Art. 5). Hubs share threat information under consortium agreements (Art. 6), participating Member States must ensure security of the network (Art. 8), and the ECCC co-procures tools with Union contributions of up to 50% or 75% of acquisition costs (Art. 9). Second, a Cybersecurity Emergency Mechanism with coordinated preparedness testing and other preparedness actions (Arts. 12-13); an EU Cybersecurity Reserve of response services from trusted managed security service providers, overseen by the Commission and possibly entrusted to ENISA, with provider selection criteria (Arts. 14-17); grants for mutual assistance (Art. 18); and support for DEP-associated third countries only under Council implementing acts (Art. 19). Third, a European Cybersecurity Incident Review Mechanism under which ENISA reviews specific significant incidents (Art. 21). The regulation also contains information, reporting and conflict-of-rules provisions (Arts. 6, 15, 16, 16a), a delegated power over reserve services (Art. 23), and an evaluation due by 5 February 2027 (Art. 25). It applies from the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal (Art. 26).

‘Cross-Border Cyber Hub’ means a multi-country platform, established by a written consortium agreement that brings together in a coordinated network structure National Cyber Hubs from at least three Member States

‘Hosting Consortium’ means a consortium composed of participating Member States, that have agreed to establish and to contribute to the acquisition of tools, infrastructure or services for, and the operation of, a Cross-Border Cyber Hub;
A National Cyber Hub shall be a single entity acting under the authority of a Member State.
‘CSIRT’ means a CSIRT designated or established pursuant to Article 10 of Directive (EU) 2022/2555;
‘entity’ means an entity as defined in Article 6, point (38), of Directive (EU) 2022/2555;

definitions.term: entities operating in sectors of high criticality

evidence.quote: ‘entities operating in sectors of high criticality’ means the types of entity listed in Annex I to Directive (EU) 2022/2555;

definitions.term: entities operating in other critical sectors

evidence.quote: ‘entities operating in other critical sectors’ means the types of entity listed in Annex II to Directive (EU) 2022/2555;
‘incident’ means an incident as defined in Article 6, point (6), of Directive (EU) 2022/2555;
‘significant cybersecurity incident’ means an incident fulfilling the criteria set out in Article 23(3) of Directive (EU) 2022/2555;
‘major incident’ means a major incident as defined in Article 3, point (8), of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2023/2841
‘large-scale cybersecurity incident’ means a large-scale cybersecurity incident as defined in Article 6, point (7), of Directive (EU) 2022/2555;
in the case of DEP-associated third countries, an incident which causes a level of disruption that exceeds the capacity of the DEP-associated third country concerned to respond to it

‘DEP-associated third country’ means a third country which is party to an agreement with the Union allowing for its participation in the Digital Europe Programme pursuant to Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2021/694;
‘contracting authority’ means the Commission or, to the extent that the operation and administration of the EU Cybersecurity Reserve has been entrusted to ENISA pursuant to Article 14(5), ENISA;
‘managed security service provider’ means a managed security service provider as defined in Article 6, point (40), of Directive (EU) 2022/2555;
‘trusted managed security service providers’ means managed security service providers selected to be included in the EU Cybersecurity Reserve in accordance with Article 17.

evidence.quote: The Commission shall have overall responsibility for the implementation of the EU Cybersecurity Reserve.

obligations.summary: The Commission may adopt delegated acts specifying the types and number of response services required for the EU Cybersecurity Reserve.

evidence.quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 23 to supplement this Regulation by specifying the types and the number of response services required

obligations.summary: Users of the EU Cybersecurity Reserve take all appropriate measures to mitigate the effects of the incident and assist recovery.

evidence.quote: the users referred to in Article 14(3) shall take all appropriate measures to mitigate the effects of the incident for which the support is requested

obligations.summary: Support requests are transmitted to the contracting authority by the route set per user type; requests must include the information listed in Art. 15(5), covering the affected entity, impact, requested service and mitigation measures.

evidence.quote: Requests for support shall be transmitted to the contracting authority as follows:

obligations.summary: For requests from Member State cyber crisis authorities and CSIRTs, Member States inform the CSIRTs network and, where appropriate, EU-CyCLONe about the requests.
obligations.conditional_on: In the case of requests from the users referred to in Article 14(3), point (a)

evidence.quote: Member States shall inform the CSIRTs network

obligations.summary: ENISA, in cooperation with the Commission and EU-CyCLONe, develops a template to facilitate requests for support.

evidence.quote: ENISA, in cooperation with the Commission and EU-CyCLONe, shall develop a template to facilitate the submission of requests for support

obligations.summary: The Commission may, by implementing acts, specify detailed procedural arrangements for requesting and responding to EU Cybersecurity Reserve support, under the examination procedure.

evidence.quote: The Commission may, by means of implementing acts, specify further the detailed procedural arrangements

obligations.summary: The contracting authority assesses requests and transmits a response within 48 hours; it assesses duration and nature of support by stated criteria; where requests are concurrent, the contracting authority and ENISA prioritise them and ENISA uses ENISA-prepared templates for agreements.
obligations.conditional_on: In the case of requests from users referred to in Article 14(3), points (a) and (b)

evidence.quote: requests for support from the EU Cybersecurity Reserve shall be assessed by the contracting authority.

obligations.summary: All parties involved limit use and sharing of information received under the Reserve to what is necessary, handle confidential or classified information only in accordance with law, and use secure information-sharing protocols including TLP.

evidence.quote: limit the use and sharing of that information to what is necessary to discharge their obligations or functions under this Regulation

obligations.summary: Service agreements between trusted managed security service providers and users must include liability conditions.

evidence.quote: All agreements referred to in this paragraph shall include, inter alia, liability conditions.

obligations.summary: Users may use Reserve services only to support response to and recovery from significant, large-scale or large-scale-equivalent incidents, and only in respect of the entities listed in Art. 16(8)(a) and (b).

evidence.quote: They may use those services only in respect of:

obligations.summary: Users that received support provide a summary report on the service, results and lessons learned to the Commission, ENISA, and the relevant networks or institutions.
obligations.applies_from: Within 2 months of the end of a support

evidence.quote: Within 2 months of the end of a support, users that have received support shall provide a summary report about the service provided

obligations.summary: The contracting authority reports to the NIS Cooperation Group, and the Commission reports to the Council and informs the High Representative, on use and results of support, at least twice per year.

evidence.quote: the contracting authority shall report to the NIS Cooperation Group, on a regular basis and at least twice per year, about the use and the results of the support.

obligations.summary: Where operation is entrusted to ENISA, ENISA reports to and consults the Commission on a regular basis and immediately sends it requests received from third-country users.
obligations.conditional_on: Where the operation and administration of the EU Cybersecurity Reserve has been entrusted to ENISA

evidence.quote: ENISA shall report to and consult the Commission on a regular basis in that respect.

obligations.summary: In procuring Reserve services, the contracting authority acts under the Financial Regulation principles and includes the criteria and requirements in Art. 17(2) in the procurement documents.
obligations.conditional_on: In procedures for establishing the EU Cybersecurity Reserve

evidence.quote: When procuring services for the EU Cybersecurity Reserve, the contracting authority shall include in the procurement documents the following criteria and requirements:

obligations.summary: Selected providers must demonstrate personnel integrity and competence, comply with classified-information rules, have a transparent governance structure, hold adequate security clearance and IT security, use hardware and software without known exploitable vulnerabilities, and meet service-delivery, language and conversion requirements (Art. 17(2)(a)-(k)); certification under a future EU scheme must follow within 2 years of that scheme's application.
obligations.conditional_on: Provider selected for the EU Cybersecurity Reserve

evidence.quote: the provider shall demonstrate that its personnel has the highest degree of professional integrity

obligations.summary: The contracting authority in procuring Reserve services applies the principles of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509 and the Art. 17(1) principles on deployability, essential security interests and Union added value.

evidence.quote: the contracting authority shall act in accordance with the principles laid down in Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509

obligations.summary: A DEP-associated third country's association agreement must include provisions requiring compliance with the obligations in Art. 19(2) and (9).
obligations.conditional_on: Where the agreement through which the third country is associated to the DEP provides for participation in the EU Cybersecurity Reserve

evidence.quote: That agreement shall include provisions requiring the DEP-associated third country concerned to comply with the obligations set out in paragraphs 2 and 9 of this Article.

obligations.summary: A DEP-associated third country provides the Commission information on its cyber resilience and risk management capabilities, updated at least once a year.
obligations.applies_from: Within 3 months of the conclusion of the agreement referred to in paragraph 1 and in any event prior to receiving any support

evidence.quote: the DEP-associated third country shall provide to the Commission information about its cyber resilience and risk management capabilities

obligations.summary: The Commission assesses at least once a year whether each DEP-associated third country complies with its agreement, has taken adequate preparedness steps, and whether support is consistent with Union policy; it consults the High Representative and, if all conditions are met, proposes a Council implementing act.

evidence.quote: The Commission shall assess regularly, and at least once a year, the following criteria in respect of each DEP-associated third country referred to in paragraph 1:

obligations.summary: The Council acts expeditiously and, as a rule, adopts implementing acts on support to third countries within eight weeks of the Commission proposal; implementing acts apply for at most one year and may be renewed.
obligations.applies_from: within eight weeks of the adoption of the relevant Commission proposal

evidence.quote: the Council shall act expeditiously and shall, as a rule, adopt the implementing acts referred to in this paragraph within eight weeks of the adoption of the relevant Commission proposal

obligations.summary: When acting under Art. 19, the Council applies the Art. 19(3) criteria and explains its assessment; where it acts on its own initiative, it explains the significant change.

evidence.quote: the Council shall apply the criteria referred to in paragraph 3, first subparagraph, and shall explain its assessment of those criteria.

obligations.summary: Support from the EU Cybersecurity Reserve to a DEP-associated third country complies with any specific conditions in the association agreement.

evidence.quote: Support from the EU Cybersecurity Reserve to a DEP-associated third country shall comply with any specific conditions laid down in the agreement referred to in paragraph 1.

obligations.summary: Each DEP-associated third country eligible for Reserve support designates an authority to act as single point of contact.
obligations.conditional_on: Each DEP-associated third country eligible for support from the EU Cybersecurity Reserve

evidence.quote: shall designate an authority to act as a single point of contact for the purposes of this Regulation.

obligations.summary: Support to a third country may be provided by the contracting authority only where, and for as long as, a Council implementing act authorising it is in force.
obligations.conditional_on: Council implementing act authorising such support is in force

evidence.quote: The contracting authority may provide support to a third country only where, and for so long as, a Council implementing act authorising such support

obligations.summary: Upon receiving a third-country support request, the Commission immediately informs the Council, keeps it informed of the assessment, and cooperates with the High Representative.
obligations.conditional_on: Upon receipt of a request for support under this Article

evidence.quote: the Commission shall immediately inform the Council.

obligations.summary: Support for a large-scale incident handled under the IPCR Arrangements is handled in accordance with their relevant procedures.
obligations.conditional_on: Where the EU Integrated Political Crisis Response Arrangements under Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/1993 (IPCR Arrangements) are activated

evidence.quote: shall be handled in accordance with the relevant procedures under the IPCR Arrangements.

obligations.summary: On request of the Commission or EU-CyCLONe, ENISA reviews and assesses a specific incident and delivers an incident review report to EU-CyCLONe, the CSIRTs network, Member States and the Commission; it gathers stakeholder feedback, ensures the report complies with protection rules and anonymises it on request; consulted representatives must disclose conflicts of interest.
obligations.conditional_on: At the request of the Commission or EU-CyCLONe

evidence.quote: ENISA shall deliver an incident review report to EU-CyCLONe, the CSIRTs network, the Member States concerned and the Commission

obligations.summary: The Commission ensures in the Reserve implementation that the Commission and ENISA carry out operation as set out in the amended Regulation 2021/694 (Art. 6(2) as replaced).

evidence.quote: However, the EU Cybersecurity Reserve shall be implemented by the Commission and, in accordance with Article 14(6) of Regulation (EU) 2025/38, by ENISA.

obligations.summary: Power to adopt delegated acts under Art. 14(7) is conferred on the Commission for 5 years from 5 February 2025, tacitly extended; the Commission reports on the delegation at least 9 months before the period ends.

evidence.quote: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 14(7) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of 5 years from 5 February 2025.

obligations.summary: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission consults experts designated by each Member State, and notifies each delegated act simultaneously to Parliament and Council.
obligations.conditional_on: Before adopting a delegated act, or upon its adoption

evidence.quote: Before adopting a delegated act, the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State

obligations.summary: The Commission evaluates the functioning of the measures and submits a report to Parliament and Council, repeated at least every 4 years.
obligations.applies_from: By 5 February 2027 and at least every 4 years thereafter

evidence.quote: By 5 February 2027 and at least every 4 years thereafter, the Commission shall evaluate the functioning of the measures provided for in this Regulation

obligations.summary: Where appropriate, the Commission submits a legislative proposal to amend the Regulation based on the evaluation reports.
obligations.conditional_on: On the basis of the reports referred to in paragraph 1, where appropriate

evidence.quote: the Commission shall, where appropriate, submit a legislative proposal to the European Parliament and to the Council to amend this Regulation.

obligations.summary: Exchange of confidential information under the Regulation is limited to what is relevant and proportionate, preserves confidentiality and does not supply information contrary to essential national interests.

evidence.quote: The sharing or exchange of information under this Regulation that is confidential pursuant to Union or national rules shall be limited to that which is relevant and proportionate

enforcement.note: No penalty, fine, criminal sanction, licence revocation, benefit clawback, suspension or blocking provision found in the operative provisions (Arts 1-26 and Annex). Recitals 14 and 36 state that National Cyber Hubs and Member States are neither obliged nor empowered by this Regulation to enforce certain requests.
